extracted.intended_audience: scientists and professional readers of Nature (naturalists, malacologists, sanitarians, astronomers, water engineers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance and implicit criteria used when reviewing or assessing scientific books, catalogues, and research articles (natural history, public health, mathematics, astronomy). Emphasizes provenance, methods, illustrations, scope, and applicability to practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor/author critical acumen and careful sifting
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of a work depends on an editor's or author's 'critical acumen and extensive knowledge' and on matter being 'carefully sifted'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An editor who carefully selects and evaluates material raises the work's trustworthiness and makes it a 'valuable repertory of facts'; critical judgement in choosing extracts and notes affects the usefulness of a catalogue or edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and provenance of specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens (eggs, etc.) supplied by dealers or third parties must be authenticated and their provenance considered; e.g., eggs from M. Favrier later 'proved to be genuine on comparison' with well-identified specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors and cataloguers should indicate sources, and where possible verify specimens by comparison with well-identified material; provenance influences how specimens are regarded and valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition of specimens affecting representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The present condition of specimens may 'not justify' additional illustration or figuration (editor regrets that condition prevents further figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about illustrating additional specimens should account for their physical condition; poor condition may preclude accurate representation even if specimens are taxonomically important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality, quantity, and suitability of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations are of two kinds (figures of eggs and lithographic landscapes); some plates (e.g., Balcombe's plates of raptorial eggs) are 'very successful', while others (Passerines) are less so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should judge both the technical success of figures and whether the mix and number of illustrations suit the work's purpose; landscapes and maps can 'add greatly to the interest' by contextualizing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and geographic/topographic coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection's value depends on the range and coverage of material (dates, regions exploited, e.g., upper basins of the Muonio and Ounas Joki), and maps/topography that help readers locate notable finds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide maps and clear geographic information; collectors and reviewers should note gaps in geographic coverage (species whose nesting-places lie east of the White Sea were not procured) and indicate where further work may be impossible or needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, brevity, and readability for intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Cambridge tracts are 'intended to help students by providing brief and readable introductions' to important theories not in ordinary textbooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability and whether the exposition is suitably brief and accessible for the target audience (students, practitioners); a good tract should stimulate follow-up study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of approach and substantive contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are judged by whether they are 'planned on novel lines' or 'add largely to the store of information' (e.g., establishing new genera, revealing breeding habits of species).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the book/paper introduces new methods, formulae, taxonomic changes, or discoveries that substantially extend knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency and stated assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses (e.g., formulae to 'calculate the allowable depreciation due to sanitary quality') must state assumptions and be explicit about limitations; the author is 'quite alive to the fact that local and other conditions must modify his conclusions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check that methods are transparent, assumptions are declared, and limitations are acknowledged; formulae intended for practical use must include discussion of how local conditions affect applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability and usefulness to practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A work's merit includes its utility to relevant professionals: e.g., 'the book is suggestive and stimulating reading' and is recommended to the 'sanitarian and water engineer'; bacteriological text is 'a trustworthy and useful guide' to medical officers and analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the content directly supports practitioners' needs (methods, calculations, interpretation guidance) and whether it is recommendable for specific professional roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and clarity of methods and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Valuable works provide 'full details of the methods employed' and chapters on 'the interpretation of results' are particularly recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether experimental/analytical procedures are described in sufficient detail for replication and whether guidance on interpreting outcomes is included and clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography and references
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'full bibliography is appended' and adds to a work's value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive references strengthen a work's utility and allow readers to trace sources and follow up; their presence is a positive evaluation point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A catalogue that 'shows no arrangement of subject' makes synoptic view difficult because notes appear in the order written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether material is organized logically for reader use; poor arrangement can impede accessibility even if content is valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample representativeness and geographic/sample limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses based on samples 'taken in limited regions' must note 'there is a possibility of unexpected deviations from theory in the at present unexplored regions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When generalizing from sampled data, reviewers should evaluate the geographic and sampling coverage and caution against overgeneralization where sampling is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical/analytical rigor and fit to observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical curves and decompositions (e.g., combining two drifts to fit observed distribution) should match observed distributions closely; discrepancies should be characterized as accidental or meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that mathematical models are appropriate, that parameters are interpretable (velocities, directions), and that model fit is demonstrated; small residuals should be judged for significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quantity and explicit counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting numbers (e.g., number of stars, eggs, specimens) and noting proportions (e.g., drifts divide stars 'nearly equally') supports conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether sample sizes are sufficient for claimed inferences and whether counts/proportions are presented transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and comparative verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons with previous work and editions (e.g., Hewitson's editions, Tristram's Algerian party) are used to verify identifications and contextualize discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether new claims are corroborated by historical records or independent collections, and whether prior literature has been appropriately consulted for validation.
